title: Find Consecutive Activity Streaks (Islands Problem)
description:
Find each consecutive streak (island) of daily user activity. Return the start date, end date, and length of each streak per user.

**Table: user_activity** — `user_id`, `activity_date`

Output columns: `user_id`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `streak_length`. Order by `user_id`, `start_date`.
solution_sql: WITH diffs AS (SELECT user_id, activity_date, activity_date - LAG(activity_date) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY activity_date) AS day_diff FROM user_activity), flagged AS (SELECT *, SUM(CASE WHEN day_diff IS NULL OR day_diff > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY activity_date) AS island_id FROM diffs) SELECT user_id, MIN(activity_date) AS start_date, MAX(activity_date) AS end_date, COUNT(*) AS streak_length FROM flagged GROUP BY user_id, island_id ORDER BY user_id, start_date

test_cases.description: User 1 has 2 streaks: Jan 1-3 (length 3) and Jan 7-8 (length 2). User 2 has 2 streaks: Jan 5-6 (length 2) and Jan 10 (length 1). Total 4 rows.

hints: First compute day_diff = activity_date minus the previous activity_date using LAG; a NULL or value > 1 means a new island starts.
Use SUM(CASE WHEN new_island THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY activity_date) to assign a monotonically increasing island_id.
explanation: Step 1: diffs CTE computes the gap to the previous date per user using LAG. Step 2: flagged CTE marks new island boundaries (day_diff IS NULL or > 1) and uses a running SUM to assign island_id. Step 3: GROUP BY user_id, island_id to collapse each island into one row with MIN/MAX dates and COUNT. User 1 has two islands; User 2 has two islands. Total: 4 rows.
